primary_task: Build, review or refactor an ASP.NET Core application following current Microsoft guidance, using the skill's reference files to choose the app model and pipeline.

requirements.name: .NET SDK (dotnet, dotnet new)
requirements.evidence: When generating new code, start from the correct `dotnet new` template and keep the generated structure recognizable.
requirements.basis: bash: install packages from the open registries (... apt from Ubuntu, ... nuget ...); Microsoft download hosts are not on the allow-list, so only an Ubuntu-packaged SDK is obtainable

requirements.name: .NET 10 / ASP.NET Core 10 target
requirements.evidence: prefer .NET 10 / ASP.NET Core 10 for new production work
requirements.basis: Ubuntu apt archive SDK versions are not stated; a preference, not a must, and the repository may pin another target

requirements.name: Microsoft Learn (verify latest features)
requirements.evidence: When a task mentions "latest", verify the feature on Microsoft Learn or the ASP.NET Core docs repo before relying on memory.
requirements.basis: lacks: network access to hosts outside the egress allow-list ... Microsoft Learn and Azure endpoints (alternative: the docs repo on GitHub is open)

requirements.name: ASP.NET Core docs repo on GitHub
requirements.evidence: Microsoft Learn or the ASP.NET Core docs repo
requirements.basis: description: GitHub (github.com, api.github.com, raw.githubusercontent.com) ... are open

requirements.name: bundled references/*.md files
requirements.evidence: Open [references/stack-selection.md](references/stack-selection.md) first for new apps or major refactors.
requirements.basis: skill: load an installed Claude Code skill; presence of bundled references not stated

requirements.name: ask_user (confirm target framework)
requirements.evidence: Confirm the target framework, SDK, and current app model.
requirements.basis: ask_user: ask the user a question (with options) and read the answer in the conversation

notes: Writing and reviewing code is done by the agent; the dotnet SDK is a start-from preference, so no requirement is hard. If dotnet were required and only an older Ubuntu SDK is reachable it would still not be unavailable. Microsoft Learn is one of two alternatives; the GitHub docs repo is reachable.
